findings.claim: success plain record -> structuredContent; conditions say plain record
findings.correction: Source guard is typeof result === object && result !== null && !Array.isArray(result); it does not check prototype/plain-object shape. Say non-null non-array objects, with raw object structural content. Keep any narrowing/schema validation conditional, not accepted behavior. JSON.stringify may throw or return undefined for widened unknown domain; no complete client validity proof from this guard.

evidence.note: Comment says plain; implementation only excludes null and arrays.

findings.claim: accessors mirror JS predicates; js_string host String-like rendering; bracket scan avoids serde rejection before Can depth
findings.correction: Keep ASCII-only obj_get key domain explicit (units_eq compares key UTF16 count to UTF8 text.len and bytes). js_string array recursion is a finite observed algorithm, not general String(Array) parity: Node::Null within Arr emits null, whereas JS array join null element becomes empty. Bracket scan enforces its own MAX_BRACKET_NESTING heuristic; it cannot guarantee all deeper legal tagged-tree input reaches decode_node if serde recursion rejects first. No change selected.

evidence.note: Null emits null and arrays recursively use js_string then join.
Pre-scan separate bracket gate followed by serde then tree decoder.
